usage: This is the standard, everyday way to ask someone's name in Cairo. It is used casually among peers, children, or in informal settings. When speaking to someone older or in a professional context, Egyptians typically add the polite pronoun 7adretak before the phrase.

variants.label: To a man
variants.note: Used when speaking to a single male peer.

variants.label: To a woman
variants.note: Used when speaking to a single female peer.

variants.label: To a group
variants.note: Used when addressing two or more people.

variants.label: Formal to a man
variants.note: Used for older men, customers, or figures of authority.

variants.label: Formal to a woman
variants.note: Used for older women, customers, or figures of authority.

examples.arabic: لَوْ سَمَحْت يَا أَفَنْدِم، حَضْرِتَك اِسْمَك إِيه؟
examples.transliteration: law sama7t ya afandim, 7adretak ismak eih?
examples.english: Excuse me sir, what is your name?
